newsitem.title: UK: NatWest declines comment on Abbey merger talk.
newsitem.headline: NatWest declines comment on Abbey merger talk.

text.p: Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc declined comment on Sunday on a newspaper report that it had discussed a 25 billion stg merger with Abbey National Plc.
"NatWest has been linked with up to 25 companies in newspaper reports over the past 12-18 months," said a NatWest spokesman. "It is our policy never to comment on market rumour or speculation."
A report in the Sunday Telegraph said NatWest had approached Abbey to discuss merging to create a financial services giant. It said Abbey had rejected the idea after "tentatively exploring" it.

The newspaper said discussions had been held at the highest level, with NatWest represented by chairman Lord Alexander and chief executive Derek Wanless and Abbey by chairman Lord Tugendhat and chief executive Peter Birch.
However, Abbey deputy chief executive Charles Toner attempted to play down the speculation.
"I can confirm that there are no talks going on between ourselves and NatWest and we are definitely not interested in talking to them," he told the Sunday Telegraph.
The newspaper quoted an "insider" as saying the deal was not off "but it is in a bit of limbo".
